## What I did

**Dataset.** [DANDI:000044](https://dandiarchive.org/dandiset/000044) (Grosmark & Buzsáki 2016, the `hc-11` recordings): bilateral silicon-probe recordings from dorsal CA1 of four Long-Evans rats, each session a PRE sleep epoch, a novel MAZE running epoch, and a POST sleep epoch. I used the five linear-track sessions (four on a 1.6 m track, one on 2 m) and excluded the three circular-platform sessions so a single linear coordinate means the same thing everywhere. Files are 5 to 9 GB each and were streamed through LINDI with a local chunk cache; nothing was downloaded in full.

**Analysis.** Running periods (speed above 5 cm/s, position tracked) split by travel direction; occupancy-normalized rate maps in 2 cm bins via `nap.compute_tuning_curves`; Skaggs spatial information tested against a 500-shuffle circular-shift null; cross-validated Bayesian decoding with `nap.decode_bayes` (odd traversals train, even traversals decode, and vice versa).

**Result.** 248 of 302 active CA1 pyramidal cells (82%) had a reliable place field in at least one direction. Median field width at half maximum was 24 cm, median spatial information 0.65 bits/spike. Fields were strongly direction selective (median |DI| 0.38): sorting the population by rightward peak gives a clean diagonal for rightward runs and an unstructured map for leftward runs over the same cells. The decoder recovered position on held-out traversals to a median error of 10 cm against a 47 cm chance level, with error falling monotonically as cells were added.

## Two things worth flagging about the source files

The position `TimeSeries` store the sampling *period* (0.0256 s) in the `rate` field, not the rate, so the timebase has to be rebuilt as `starting_time + arange(n) * rate`. The pipeline asserts that `n_samples * rate` matches the MAZE epoch duration. Separately, the linearized coordinate is NaN whenever the animal is off the track proper, so only 13 to 32% of MAZE samples carry a usable position. I tried extending the linearization by fitting the affine map from the raw x coordinate and applying it to all on-track samples, but the extra samples fall almost entirely in the stationary reward zones and are removed by the speed filter anyway, so I dropped that and used the authors' curation directly.

## Files

- `place_cells_dandi000044.py` — jupytext notebook, runs end to end
- `place_cells_dandi000044.ipynb` — executed, 15 code cells, no errors, 7 inline figures
- `place_cells_lib.py` — loading, rate maps, statistics, shuffling helpers
- `figures/fig01` through `fig07` — session overview, behaviour and LFP with theta, example place cells, population tiling, statistics, decoding, cross-session summary
- `README.md`, `session_summary.csv`, `results_summary.json`

The notebook imports `place_cells_lib.py`, so the two need to sit together. A cold run takes about 13 minutes; with a warm LINDI cache it is under 4.
